# Shared roofs: bounded anchors, genuine slabs, and actual facet base-rank reduction

There are three separate conclusions. First, even a bounded shared roof
does not put all selector laws into ordinary caps of one convex lift.
Second, there is an exact affine-gauge boundedness lemma when one common
set of anchors is controlled. Third, ACTUAL proper source caps on one
global ambient facet force a strict reduction in integer-coordinate rank.
The last conclusion applies to each genuine one-height selector lift;
it does not yet transfer its center or allocate its credit globally.

## 1. Two positive selectors already obstruct a common ordinary-cap lift

This sharpens the bounded-roof example communicated by Rate. Take

    r(x)=-x^2 on [-1,1],
    tau_1(x)=clamp(r(x)+2,0,1)=1,
    tau_2(x)=clamp(r(x)+1,0,1)=1-x^2.

These are the lengths of the genuine unit slabs [-2,-1] and [-1,0]
below the SAME concave roof. Both have positive total mass.

There is no convex vertical body whose upward cap lengths at the ACTUAL
two slab-floor heights -2 and -1 equal tau_1 and tau_2 at every x. Indeed
at x=+-1 the requested lengths are (1,0). Its closed vertical interval
must therefore contain height-2 and end at height-1. Convexity forces
(0,-2) into the middle fiber. At x=0 the requested lengths are (1,1),
so its interval has positive length above-1 and no length between-2 and-1.
That contradicts containing (0,-2). A common affine vertical shear or
translation cannot remove the contradiction: it preserves convexity and
all the corresponding actual cap inequalities.

The same test preserves sampled boundary bases exactly. Set x=z and
sample z=-1,0,1. The actual convex mixed body

    C_delta={(z,y): -1<=z<=1, -2<=y<=-delta z^2}

has positive d=1 fibers on this complete three-point base. Its limiting
top ambient facet has scaled common roof r. Taking physical smoothing
width delta, cap thresholds -delta and0 give precisely these two boundary
selectors. (The slab floors are threshold/delta minus1.) The two endpoint
bases cannot be discarded as ambient-surface null. This is an actual
compatible roof construction, not an assertion that these caps form a
deepest-source menu. No divergence is present, so a proposed dichotomy
whose bounded branch requires ordinary CAP lifts is false at its first
branch. Genuine SLABS remain valid.

## 2. An exact anchored affine-gauge boundedness lemma

Let G=conv{v_1,...,v_k} be a compact polytope in its own affine hull and
choose w=sum_i lambda_i v_i with every lambda_i>0 and sum lambda_i=1.
Write lambda_min=min lambda_i. Let rho_l be any concave functions on G
(for example a common roof after subtracting ONE affine function). If

    rho_l(v_i)>=-L for every i,l, and rho_l(w)<=U,

then throughout G

    -L<=rho_l(x)<=(U+L)/lambda_min-L.                 (1)

Proof: the lower bound is concavity. Express x=sum mu_i v_i. Put
theta=min_{mu_i>0} lambda_i/mu_i; then theta>=lambda_min, theta<=1,
and w=theta x+(1-theta)y for some y in G. Consequently
U>=rho_l(w)>=theta rho_l(x)-(1-theta)L. This proves (1).

This lemma includes anchors on every sampled boundary base. A fixed
finite collection of compact polytopal own-facet patches may be used for
G; the vertices of all patches are anchors. No ambient integration is
used to erase boundary-base information.

One sufficient selector condition is a SINGLE cap whose unsaturated
arguments are controlled at all v_i and at w. If

    tau_l=clamp(1+alpha_l r_l+ell_l,0,1),
    alpha_l>=alpha_min>0,

and all these finitely many selector values lie strictly between0 and1,
then rho_l=r_l+ell_l/alpha_l has values between -1/alpha_min and0 there.
Formula (1) bounds the whole normalized roof. Uniform separation from0
and1 is not needed for this boundedness conclusion.

If each additional cap's affine correction after this SAME gauge is
bounded at an affine spanning anchor set, and its positive alpha is
bounded above/below, all its unit-slab floor and ceiling functions are
bounded. One sufficiently low common constant floor then gives a bounded
convex hypograph body carrying those genuine slab intersections. This is
an exact compactness criterion, not a claim that positive selector mass
alone supplies its anchor hypotheses.

## 3. Why positive masses and transition records do not alone bound the roof

On the continuous interval [-1,1], let L increase to infinity and set

    r_L(x)=-L|x|,
    g_+(x)=1/2+L(x-|x|),
    g_-(x)=1/2-L(x+|x|),
    tau_+-=clamp(g_+-,0,1).

The two g's share the SAME roof and differ by affine functions. Their
selector limits are (1/2)1_(x>=0) and (1/2)1_(x<=0), up to the common
midpoint, so both have positive mass. Yet no single affine function eta_L
makes r_L-eta_L uniformly bounded: its affine-invariant midpoint defect is

    r_L(0)-[r_L(-1)+r_L(1)]/2=L.

These are compatible actual roofs: take physical strip width delta_L=L^-2
and actual upper roof delta_L r_L=-|x|/L above the fixed lower plane
-sqrt(12). Normals with tangential slopes +-1/L and thresholds delta_L/2
produce the displayed arguments. Their covariance norms Gamma_L agree by
reflection and tend to1; the normalized construction uses h_L=delta_L/Gamma_L
and divides normals and thresholds by Gamma_L. Thus all stated limiting
S and A/h constants below use the actual Gamma=1 convention. A product
with any fixed lattice-convex base
retains all of its sampled boundary bases. The two physical cap budgets
are equal by reflection, but these near-outside caps are NOT claimed to
be active at actual deepest sources.

Their surviving selector supports are full-dimensional half intervals,
not proper exposed faces of the ORIGINAL interval. After normalizing
r_L by L they do correspond to the two exposed graph faces of the NEW
tent hypograph. Thus any valid divergent-scale induction must specify
that new geometry and retain its residual slab heights; it cannot simply
delete the interiors of the old facet.

The additional width records do not by themselves exclude this example.
On the surviving half interval, tau=1/2 and chi=1; hence
integral tau(1-tau)=1/4 per unit base fiber. For an outside support the
actual uniform-kernel signed cost is

    A/h+S/2=-[integral tau(1-tau)]/(2|u|) -> -1/8.

Here S->1/2 and A/h->-3/8. The capwise transition PSD is automatic because
there is only outside transition mass. These exact records therefore do
not convert this roof-only construction into a bounded-gauge conclusion.
This is a scoped test: the missing actual source/global-stationarity
constraints could still rule it out in a minimizing sequence.

## 4. Actual ambient-facet incidence gives a strict base-rank drop

Now impose ACTUAL retained source-cap geometry. Let C be the limiting
canonical convex body and let its global ambient facet lie in

    F: a_F.z+n_F.x=b_F,       n_F!=0,

with C on the <= side. Let Y=(p,y) be a retained source with a uniform own
inball and let an actual retained cap have normal N=(a,u), threshold

    c=N.Y-b,   b>=0,

where b=0 for buffer-free smoothing and b is small in the H setting.
Assume it supports a positive own-facet patch belonging to F. Then its
continuous normal has the form u=s alpha n_F, alpha>0, s in {+1,-1}.
On F its margin depends only on base:

    N.(z,x)-c=lambda(z),
    lambda(z)=(a-s alpha a_F).z+s alpha b_F-c.         (2)

Every sampled base where this cap supports its F-facet satisfies lambda=0.
But its own source does not. Put

    t_F=b_F-a_F.p-n_F.y>0.

The own inball gives t_F>=r_s |n_F|. Equation (2) gives exactly

    lambda(p)=s alpha t_F+b.                          (3)

For s=+1 this is strictly positive. For s=-1 it is strictly negative
whenever b<alpha r_s |n_F|, as supplied by uniform own properness/small
buffer. Thus lambda is not identically zero on the full base affine hull.
All supporting sampled bases of THIS cap on THIS ambient facet lie in
the proper affine section

    H={z:lambda(z)=0},                                (4)

which excludes its own source. This conclusion does not require bounded
scaled roofs, affine cap-tilt limits divided by h, or an exposed base face.

The section in (4) need not be an exposed face of conv(P). For example a
slanted cap may cross the projection of F, with some other bases strictly
inside its captured side and some strictly outside. A face-based induction
must not strengthen (4) to an exposed-face assertion without further data.

## 5. Correct induced lattice and a genuine lower-integer-rank selector lift

Let P_FH be the finite sampled integer bases actually used by the facet
patches in (4). If it is nonempty, fix p0 in P_FH and put

    V=span_R{p-p0:p in P_FH}, r=dim V<=n-1,
    Lambda=V intersect Z^n.

Although lambda may have irrational coefficients, V is spanned by integer
vectors. Hence V is rational and Lambda is a full-rank lattice in V.
To check this directly, select r independent integer difference vectors.
They span a discrete subgroup of rank r contained in Lambda; discreteness
of Z^n bounds the other inclusion, so Lambda has rank r as well. Choosing
a lattice basis identifies p0+Lambda with Z^r by an affine map. One must
use Lambda, not merely the subgroup generated by the listed differences,
which can have nontrivial index.

Convexification does not lose lattice completeness: every integer point
of conv(P_FH) lies in the original complete base and in H. Before taking
limits, enlarge the finite sampled list to EVERY integer base in the
projection of the compact patch hull G. At each such base take the ACTUAL
selector-lift trace, which may be empty or lower-dimensional. Do not insert
an artificial zero trace where anchored compatibility forces a nonempty
one, and do not delete positive traces by their ambient measure. All
integer bases of the canonical hull are now included in the induced lattice.

Write F by coordinates (z,tangent x), using an affine base-dependent
continuous translation to remove a_F.z. For the actual shared-roof
sequence, each cap's individual unit-height lift is convex in

    (z,tangent x,t),  z in p0+V,  0<=t<=1.

It has r integer coordinates and d continuous coordinates: d-1 tangent
coordinates plus the ONE uniform-kernel height. Its sampled traces have
exactly the cap's genuine selector volumes. Work on compact polytopal
patches, retain a Hausdorff limit of each finite sampled trace, and pass
every anchored Minkowski inclusion. The canonical convex hull of these
limiting traces has exactly those traces, since anchored compatibility
gives containment for every convex combination landing at an integer base.
Thus this constructs an ACTUAL compatible mixed convex body in dimensions

    (r,d),   r<=n-1,                                  (5)

not a projected density with guessed concavity. Exhausting the patches
retains the full desired facet law. Projection or continuous intrinsic
dimension can drop further; then apply the established intrinsic extension
or retain the lower-dimensional stratum explicitly. No positive d-volume
is asserted for a degenerate limit.

Therefore a previously proved closed minor in the number of INTEGER
coordinates is genuinely applicable to each nondegenerate individual
selector lift. It does NOT by itself locate the minor center at Y (which
is outside H), compare its caps to the original full menu, or assign
overlapping surface credit. These are the remaining transfer obligations.

### 5.1 Global facet restriction is legitimate; interior-section isolation is not

The ambient supporting slack g_F=b_F-a_F.z-n_F.x is nonnegative on C.
For any bounded-on-C nonnegative convex test phi, the actual convex fields
[phi-t g_F]_+ restrict its boundary integral to F as t increases to infinity.
This retains the sampled boundary-base facets just as before. Thus global
ambient-facet restriction has a genuine physical-field implementation.

There is no analogous automatic localization to the base section H when
it crosses the relative interior. If w0 in H is a nontrivial convex
combination theta w_-+(1-theta)w_+ of points outside H, every nonnegative
convex physical test obeys

    Phi(w0)<=theta Phi(w_-)+(1-theta)Phi(w_+).

Consequently a family of such tests cannot converge to a positive value
at w0 while converging to0 at both endpoints. Any isolated-minor proof
must pay the resulting endpoint costs or add an actual exposed-face
hypothesis. Replacing g_F by |lambda| in the preceding localization does
not fix this: phi-t|lambda| need not be convex. This is an exact reason
why the rank reduction alone is not yet a valid localized body descent.

## 6. Extreme continuous circuits reduce overlap within a source menu

For buffer-free smoothing choose a minimal positive continuous circuit
from the actual balanced active normals. If its linear rank is r_c, its
cardinality is r_c+1. If r_c>=2 it has no repeated or antipodal normalized
continuous normals: repeated normals can be consolidated, and an antipodal
pair would already be a proper positive subcircuit. Since Gamma(u)=1,
parallel normals of the same orientation coincide, and parallel opposite
normals are antipodal.

On one fixed positive-area own-fiber facet, every supporting cap has
continuous normal parallel to its normal. Consequently at most ONE cap
from a rank-at-least-two minimal circuit can support that facet. In rank1
the circuit is exactly an antipodal pair. This is a within-source incidence
statement. It does not merge circuits from different deepest sources,
make their full ambient normals antipodal, or prove their surface budgets
disjoint after cross-source transport.

## 7. Scope of the resulting route

The exact positive result is the lower-integer-rank physical lift (5),
together with an explicit anchor criterion for a bounded common SLAB
model. The exact negative results rule out a common ordinary-CAP model
and roof-only coercivity from positive selector masses/transition costs.
The rank drop already uses actual proper source geometry. What remains
unproved is a center/credit transfer joining these closed minors to the
original simultaneous separator without charging overlaps more than once.
